classification.difficultyReason: Translate three perpendicular central cuts into a sketch of a spherical octant and distinguish its one-eighth curved surface from its three additional quarter-circle faces before combining areas.

content.prompt: A sphere of radius $2\text{ cm}$ is cut into eight equal parts with three mutually perpendicular slices through its centre. Sketch one of these parts, then find its volume and surface area.

answer.short:
$V=\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^3$, $A=5\pi\text{ cm}^2$.

A spherical octant has one-eighth of the sphere's curved surface and three quarter-circle faces.
answer.worked:
The sketch is a spherical octant with three perpendicular quarter-circle faces.
$$\begin{align*}V&=\frac{1}{8}\times\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\\V&=\frac{1}{8}\times\frac{4}{3}\pi(2)^3\\V&=\frac{4\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$
Add one-eighth of the sphere's curved area and the three exposed quarter-circle faces.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{1}{8}(4\pi r^2)+3\left(\frac{1}{4}\pi r^2\right)\\A&=\frac{1}{8}(4\pi(2)^2)+3\left(\frac{1}{4}\pi(2)^2\right)\\A&=5\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Authored sketch of a spherical octant. Three projected perpendicular radii meet at the sphere centre; each pair bounds a quarter-circle face. No decorative shading.
spec.mathematics: Octant of a radius-2 cm sphere obtained by three mutually perpendicular diametral cuts.
